# Lazulite

> Lazulite is an Android app that shows the real Bluetooth audio codec in use between your phone and your headphones, in real time.

Lazulite reads Android's Bluetooth audio stack to reveal what streaming apps and manufacturers often hide: the actual codec negotiated (LDAC, aptX, aptX HD, aptX Adaptive, aptX TWS, LC3, LHDC V1-V5, AAC, SBC, and Samsung SSC/SSC UHQ where available), packet loss, and transmission/signal quality — instead of relying on what a streaming app claims to be sending.

Key facts:
- Platform: Android only (no iOS version, no wired/desktop support — it specifically monitors the Bluetooth audio stack)
- Distribution: Google Play Store, paid app (one-time purchase, price set on the Play Store)
- Core features: real-time Bluetooth codec detection, packet loss monitoring, transmission stability metrics, signal quality analysis, and setup suggestions
- Setup: requires reading Android system audio logs, granted via ADB, Shizuku, or root access
- Privacy: all audio analysis runs locally on-device; optional anonymous crash/usage telemetry via Firebase, can be disabled in Settings

Links:

Also available in Spanish (https://lazulite.app/es/), Simplified Chinese (https://lazulite.app/zh/), and Italian (https://lazulite.app/it/).
